docSummary: Synthetic fixture for 'Agency X': a vendor supports 12 eServices (Portal through Posting, after Booklet's decommission) under a brownfield engagement, with an incumbent services team of 30-36 people and a separate 18-person platform team (different tender) running infrastructure on a hosting vendor's Singapore cloud. The FY25 summary table (April 2025-March 2026, a stated 12-month period) shows 636 total incidents (Sev A 155 / Sev B 474 / Sev C 7), 3066 SRs and 202 CRs; these were divided by 12 to get monthly figures (incidents ≈53.0/mo, SRs ≈255.5/mo, CRs ≈16.83/mo). Severity mix was mapped Sev A→P1 (24.37%), Sev B→P2 (74.53%), Sev C→P3 (1.10%), no P4 reported. Job/batch failures (92) are operational counters, not logged incidents, and were excluded. L1 is out of scope for the vendor (agency help desk); an L1.5 client-run team filters 20-30% of tickets before L2/L3, and under 5% of the remainder reaches L3. Two small separate automation opportunities (account review, log analysis) were also discussed and are listed separately, not as towers.

towers.label: eServices application support (12 eServices: Portal, Callup, Manning, Deferment, Payslip, Registration, Clearance, Pay, Awards, Leave and Claims, Retail, Posting)

opportunities.name: Account review automation
opportunities.note: ~12 man-days/month manual effort, ~5,000 accounts/month, no central database; scope later updated to 12 sources across 5 categories; standalone 2-month tool proposed, commercial approval pending.

opportunities.name: Log analysis automation
opportunities.note: Weekly manual log review, 5 use cases, handled by one person via email/Excel; candidate to plug into an AIOps pipeline later.

warnings: Sev A conflict: an earlier session stated platform-wide Sev A = 6 for FY25, but the session-4 table shows total Sev A = 155, almost entirely from Callup (140 of 155) - flagged by the bid team itself as a number to challenge; used the later table value.
Job/batch failures (total 92, e.g. Retail 54, Pay 30, Awards 8) are operational counters, not logged incidents, and were excluded from inc and mix per instructions.

Booklet eService ambiguity: session 3 says '12 eServices in total; one (Booklet) is being decommissioned', but the FY25 table already lists exactly 12 named eServices without Booklet - unclear whether Booklet is additional to or included in the 12.
Platform team (18 FTE) is described as a separate tender running infrastructure/platform - not included as a tower (out of scope for this AMS sizing).

Hosting is on public cloud in Singapore run by a separate hosting vendor - infrastructure excluded as a tower; Singapore reflects hosting location only, not confirmed bidder delivery location, so eng.region/locMix were omitted.

L1 is explicitly out of scope (agency help desk = customer). An intermediate client-run L1.5 team (3-4 people, 24x7) filters 20-30% of tickets before L2/L3; per rules this rate was not used for pass12, only the <5% L2->L3 rate was used for pass23.
Security incidents are handled by a separate enterprise team and are excluded from this tower's figures.
incumbentFTE (33) is the midpoint of the stated 30-36 person range for the incumbent services team.
Monthly inc/sr/cr figures were derived by dividing FY25 (April 2025-March 2026, a stated 12-month period) totals by 12; verify this matches the intended reporting basis.
Account-review automation scope changed between sessions from '10 systems' to '12 sources across 5 categories' - latest figure used in opportunities.
Page 5 content (6 pods, 28 FTE estimate) is explicitly an AI-generated/bid-team analysis, not client-stated fact, and was excluded entirely from extraction.
Manning data is noted as only 6 months collected with a next step to build a full 12-month baseline - the FY25 Manning row may be provisional/incomplete.
crMix was omitted: CRs are described only qualitatively ('mostly policy driven', 'time consuming') with no quantified complexity split.
User counts ('fewer than 1000 users supported', '4000 concurrent users at maximum') were not clearly identifiable as MAU, so towers.0.mau was omitted.
Coverage '8x5' is an inferred mapping of 'business hours' support; exact hours not stated.
